pll2d7c3-d1e3514.summary: States that the good have a much freer choice after confirmation than before.

pll2d7c3-d1e3519.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: they do not lack free choice because they cannot will evil; choice that cannot serve sin is much freer; the blessed will to be blessed so that they cannot even will misery.
claims: Choice that cannot serve sin is freer.

pll2d7c3-d1e3540.summary: States that good angels cannot will evil or misery, not by nature but by grace; before confirmation they could sin, and some did and became demons.

pll2d7c3-d1e3543.summary: Cites Augustine against Maximinus: heavenly creatures could die because they could sin; angels sinned and became demons, and those who did not could have; any rational creature's inability to sin is by grace, not nature; only God by nature cannot sin. So their former ability came from natural free choice, their present inability from grace, which keeps free choice from serving sin.
claims: Inability to sin in creatures comes from grace.
God alone is impeccable by nature.

pl-l2d7c3.summary: Holds that the good angels' choice is much freer after confirmation. Augustine: choice that cannot serve sin is freer; the blessed will to be blessed so that they cannot will misery. The good angels cannot will evil not by nature but by grace: before confirmation they could sin, and some did; as Augustine says, any creature's inability to sin is by God's grace, God alone being unable to sin by nature.
claims: The good angels' free choice is freer after confirmation.
Choice that cannot serve sin is freer.
The good angels cannot will evil by grace, not by nature.
Only God cannot sin by nature.
